Net neutrality means that ISPs can't prioritise traffic. Once a package is on the network it has to be treated like any other package, regardless whether it's part of an emergency services call, part of a datastream for online surgery, a stock market ticker or just someone's porn.

But ISPs still need to perform price banding, because some people can't afford the average (like me) and large businesses and critical operations will want to pay above the average to ensure a good connection. So we have bandwidth caps. You can go with their lowest cap or pay to have a higher one. This doesn't actually guarantee a stable connection, if the network is busy your data will still be processed at the same, congested, rate as anyone else's, no matter how important it is or how much you paid. Equally, if traffic is light and the network is underused, you won't be able to exceed your cap, so there's alot of wasted bandwidth. All in all, data caps are better than nothing, but they're a blunt tool and only effective under some circumstances.

The solution is to get rid of net neutrality. Now, instead of paying to have an artificial cap lifted, you're paying for priority. So when traffic is heavy and some guy is watching porn on a cheap connection, his traffic won't be prioritised over that emergency services call, the call goes through first. Equally, when the network is being lightly used, cheapo mc-pornwatcher can use all the bandwidth he likes, because no one else needs it.
